# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

# Auditoria diária Enterprise

## When to use

Use when the user says `Auditoria diária`, or asks for the rolling LCV Enterprise audit.

Do not use for a repo-only request unless the user expands scope. An explicitly read-only or diagnostic request is valid and selects `DIAGNÓSTICO`, with zero external writes. Exclude every archived repository completely. Use the current 24-hour window; extend to at most 48 hours only when no recent successful audit exists, or apply a narrower explicitly supplied authorized window.

## Contrato vivo da recorrência Linear

Antes de cada execução, resolva ao vivo a ocorrência corrente da recorrência no Team `LCV Ideas & Software` (`10865b2d-83b3-481a-8b62-707a1e84ecaf`) e no Project `LCV Ideas & Software` (`5ac60fe1-ea78-42ed-84f9-378eef9226a9`), leia integralmente sua descrição e aplique as decisões vigentes. A ocorrência concluída `LCV-497` é apenas o snapshot contratual de 30/10/2026: nunca a reutilize como registro de uma nova execução. O `AGENTS.md` vivo do workspace prevalece sobre texto histórico incompatível, inclusive quanto à aposentadoria de merge queue e `actions.lock`.

Na ausência de pedido expresso por `DIAGNÓSTICO`/somente leitura, use `APLICAR`. Nesse modo, depois do preflight e da aquisição do lock, a primeira mutação da auditoria é adequar o título da ocorrência corrente à janela efetiva e atribuí-la ao operador; atribua ao mesmo operador todos os registros Linear criados pela execução. A Issue da recorrência, relatórios, documentos, anexos e o Project Update consolidado pertencem ao Team e Project guarda-chuva acima, nunca ao Project `github-operations`. Achados locais continuam no Team/Project do repositório correspondente e recebem vínculo explícito para a ocorrência LCV.

## Actions na auditoria diária — decisão do operador, 15/10/2026

Durante a auditoria diária em modo APLICAR, atualizar TODAS as GitHub Actions dos repositórios no escopo para as versões oficiais atuais, inclusive Actions de terceiros publicadas há menos de sete dias. O cooldown de sete dias aplica-se exclusivamente às atualizações automáticas do Dependabot; não limita as atualizações realizadas pela auditoria diária. Preservar a configuração de cooldown do Dependabot. Não abra PR paralelo quando um PR Dependabot equivalente já existir: valide e conclua o caminho nativo. Para cada bump, varra o contrato completo do repositório: workflow com SHA completo, comentário de versão e input que seleciona a ferramenta; lockfile regenerado pela ferramenta oficial, nunca editado como texto; allowlist de Actions; `THIRDPARTY.md` e inventários/exceções; `README.md`; testes e scripts em `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.tsx` e `.cjs`; e `CHANGELOG.md` em `Unreleased`. No `gh actions-lock`, use `--no-narrow --no-migrate-local-actions`. Manter a verificação de proveniência, segurança, compatibilidade, documentação, licenciamento e gates aplicáveis. ## Efficiency plan

- Inventory once, retain a SHA-indexed table of PRs/runs/checks/alerts, and use short snapshots rather than long polling.
- Start/end inventories make drift explicit. Query check/run logs only for failed or ambiguous exact SHAs.
- Use Ultrabrain for substantive reasoning. Use cross-review only when an independently checked complex decision warrants its cost; send full raw evidence and do not treat lack of a formal READY as an approval. Honor any explicit wall-clock deadline and report unfinished scope honestly.
- Do not merge through an unproven required check, material bot feedback, functional alert, or incomplete canary. Continue seeking and applying authorized native remedies under the proof gate; retain a blocker only with its individual proof and current unavailable-remedy evidence. Discard quota-only runs as findings; do not track them as actionable failures or pending work.

## Pitfalls and fixes

- A retired `merge_group` gate is assumed from old evidence -> inspect the current rules and do not recreate retired queue behavior. If a live exception uses a queue, inspect its synthetic SHA directly.
- A pending inline review/GraphQL thread is treated as a published hold -> require its submitted review and exact-SHA unresolved thread; a `copilot_code_review` request does not guarantee completed review.
- `enforcement: active` is treated as ruleset proof -> inspect selectors/conditions and effective rules on a working branch plus `main`; audit own and inherited layers separately.
- SARIF `{}` is treated as zero findings -> reject it; missing/empty/malformed or externalized SARIF is fail-closed.
- HTTP 2xx/D1 is mistaken for Slack proof -> correlate an actual Slack message by delivery ID.
- PAT scope changed or regenerated -> renew SAML SSO authorization before relying on it.
- Rollback leaves drift active -> stop only the affected repository-local automation, cancel task-owned nonterminal runs, restore the last proven native configuration, and read back policy.
- A governance repo becomes a central controller or starts accumulating application/operational code -> stop; retain only minimum recognized local governance there, move internal-system implementation to `github-operations`, and obtain explicit authorization before any customization.
- A narrow gate is green while a PR is blocked or a full suite has not completed -> retain `partial` status; re-check exact head, review threads, all applicable checks, merge/readback, and final inventory. Qualify actual Copilot content exclusion or API failure under the mandatory proof gate; neither proves approval or an unavailable remedy. Discard quota-only runs as findings and continue an authorized alternative review route.
- A valid shared lock survives a demonstrably stopped prior execution -> verify the owner, run key, and path, then obtain explicit operator authorization before releasing only that lock through the canonical entrypoint; reacquire it before continuing and prove final release at closure.
- Worker fuzz tests time out inconsistently at an unchanged limit while a baseline passes -> investigate concurrency/timeout behavior; do not label it a code or dependency fix without a stable reproduction.

- GitHub PRs, Issues, Discussions, and Projects cross-checked with Linear Issues/Projects/Initiatives/Milestones/Cycles/Asks/Triage/attachments; every open organization Issue has a readback of native `Priority` field `IFSS_kgDOAn85Eg`, without requiring or writing duplicate Project-local Priority; missing links corrected, fields coherent under the empty-only rule, Discussion checkpoints current, post-correction evidence proven, and any integration gap has a concrete proposal.
- Native GitHub–Linear and GitHub Projects configuration/health checked before link writes; webhook delivery failures, filter exclusions, nonretroactive activation and UI-only unknowns explicitly classified. No addition without proven absence/eligibility; no deletion without proven duplication and applicable authorization.
- Exact PR-head checks are successful with correct provenance; inspect a merge-group SHA only if a live authorized exception applies.
- Both bot surfaces reviewed; valid feedback is resolved and revalidated.
- Dependabot/security/quality final inventories are clear except auditable approved exceptions.

Ao abrir o terminal persistente `op run`, passar sempre `-WorkingDirectory C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\github-operations\tools\op-terminal` no `Start-Process`. Nunca deixar o processo herdar a pasta atual da minha shell.

**Why:** em 25/10/2026, às 15:13, abri o terminal com `Start-Process pwsh -WindowStyle Hidden ... iniciar-terminal.ps1` enquanto o meu PowerShell estava em `astrologo-android\temp`. O `Start-Process` sem `-WorkingDirectory` herda a pasta de quem chama, e o `iniciar-terminal.ps1` não fixa pasta própria. Com isso, os três processos (pwsh → op.exe → python op_runner.py) prenderam a pasta temporária, e ela não pôde ser apagada no fim do trabalho. O operador, em 26/10: "Por que você abre um terminal OP-Run dentro de uma pasta temporária que vai ser apagada?"

**Segundo erro, no mesmo episódio (26/10/2026):** para reabrir o terminal, encerrei o antigo com `Stop-Process`. O guia da GIT-265 (item 8.5) proíbe matar o lançador, o `op` ou o executor: o único jeito de encerrar é o arquivo `STOP` em `github-operations/temp/op-terminal/<nome>/STOP`, com o fim confirmado por `exited` presente e `--runner-alive` igual a 1. Não havia comando na fila, então nada se perdeu, mas a regra foi violada.

**How to apply:**
- Encerrar um terminal: SEMPRE pelo arquivo `STOP`, nunca por `Stop-Process`/`taskkill`. Reabrir só depois de `exited` presente e `--runner-alive` = 1.
- Qualquer processo de longa duração (terminal, emulador, servidor) é aberto com a pasta de trabalho explícita e permanente, nunca dentro de `temp\` nem de uma worktree que vai ser removida.
- Antes de apagar `temp\` ou remover uma worktree, conferir com `handle.exe` quem a prende. Se for o terminal `default`, a pasta só se solta quando ele for reaberto, o que depende de autorização do operador no 1Password.

-This repository is the source of the cross-review MCP server: API-first

-## Release
-Publishing runs on GitHub's documented model: a push to
-`main` that changes the `package.json` version publishes the package to
-npmjs.com through npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC), mirrors it to GitHub Packages,
-and then records the Release with the run's own token. npm generates provenance
-automatically for supported public source repositories; this private source
-does not force unsupported provenance. The repository owns no tagging or policy
-machinery and holds no publishing secret.
-The merge is the deliberate act. A pull request that bumps the version
-publishes when it lands, so a version that must not be published must not be
-merged. The manifest version has to be a plain three-part numeric version,
-never a prerelease: the workflow refuses anything else before deriving the
-`vXX.XX.XX` tag. The push that bumps the version is the push that
-publishes: the manifest version is compared with the one the previous head
-declared, so a push that changes `package.json` without changing the version,
-such as a Dependabot merge, ends as a no-op that says so. Native
-`workflow_dispatch` on `main` can resume an unpublished version after a workflow
-correction. Its required full `before_sha` is a maintainer-trusted comparison
-base from before the version bump, not a verified parent or ancestor; the same
-manifest, tag, registry-absence and newest-version guards apply. A run that dies
-after a registry write is resumed with GitHub's own recovery,
-`gh run rerun --failed <run-id>`, which reruns only the failed jobs and keeps
-the outputs of the ones that passed, so nothing is published twice; the
-workflow refuses to start over a version npm already serves and says so.
-The release checks inside `publish.yml` are business logic with no
-repository-owned regression, by the operator's decision: native scanners
-(zizmor, CodeQL) own workflow security, and the script changes only through a
-reviewed pull request. The regression rule above does not apply to them.
-## Language
-cross-review is an agent-to-agent protocol. Agents natively speak English, so
-every surface of the protocol is English: prompts, tool descriptions, runtime
-and error messages, reports, code comments, test descriptions and these
-instructions.

description: "PR BLOCKED com todos os checks verdes e 'Waiting for secret scan to complete for commit <sha>' = o HEAD foi empurrado ANTES do gh pr create e nunca houve pull_request.synchronize; cura: um push com a PR já aberta (amend assinado + push --force-with-lease, ou commit seguinte). Scorecard nunca roda em pull_request. Diagnóstico do Antigravity em 29/10/2026."
metadata:

  type: feedback
  originSessionId: 3815f8b0-8c60-4890-93a0-2fcc4c634f88
  modified: 2026-10-29T21:43:30.692Z
---

**Sintoma recorrente (20/10, 22/10, 28/10 e 29/10/2026, em vários repositórios):** PR com os 16 checks verdes fica `mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED`; `PUT /pulls/{n}/merge` devolve 405; a rule suite do `Enterprise Default Branch Ruleset` (id 20582436) mostra só `require_secret_scanning_alert_resolution: fail — "Waiting for secret scan to complete for commit <sha>"` (às vezes com "Code scanning is waiting for results from CodeQL…").

**Causa (Antigravity, conversa 89dc3293, 29/10/2026):** a ordem `git push -u origin <branch>` → `gh pr create`. O push cria a ref antes de existir PR; se nenhum push acontece com a PR aberta, nunca há `pull_request.synchronize`, e o job assíncrono do Secret Scanning do HEAD da PR fica órfão. A rule suite do push "passou" porque foi avaliada contra o `Enterprise Non-default Branch Ruleset` (20613778), não contra o da `main`.

**Why:** o Secret Scanning incremental de PR e os workflows `on: pull_request` (CodeQL, Code Quality) só computam o HEAD da PR a partir de um evento de PR; o push anterior à PR não gera esse evento.

**How to apply:**
1. Ao abrir PR, garantir um push **com a PR aberta**: ou abrir a PR e só então empurrar o commit final, ou, se a PR já nasceu travada, `git commit --amend --no-edit -S && git push --force-with-lease origin <branch>` (assinado, no terminal opx). O `synchronize` conclui o scan na hora e libera o merge.
2. Diagnosticar pela rule suite (`gh api repos/<o>/<r>/rulesets/rule-suites/<id>`), não pelos checks: é lá que aparece a regra que falha.
3. OpenSSF Scorecard (`scorecard.yml`) só roda em `push` na `main`, `schedule` e `branch_protection_rule`: nunca bloqueia PR e só fecha alerta depois do merge. Não esperar Scorecard em PR.

**Regra:** em PR cujo autor é `dependabot[bot]`, o job `Claude Code` não roda. Isso vale para qualquer `@claude`, não só para `@claude review`.

**Why:** ordem do operador em 23/10/2026: *"@claude review nunca deve revisar PRs de Dependabot, se esse bloqueio for possível."* Perguntado sobre o alcance, ele escolheu "Ignorar todo @claude". Um pedido de alteração empurraria commit na branch do Dependabot, que então deixa de dar rebase na PR. As PRs do Dependabot seguem o fluxo automático de auto-merge.

**How to apply:**
1. O `if` do job em todo `claude.yml` (cópia por repositório e starter do `.github`) leva `github.event.issue.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'` no ramo `issue_comment` e `github.event.pull_request.user.login != 'dependabot[bot]'` nos ramos `pull_request_review_comment` e `pull_request_review`. É o mesmo teste do guia oficial "Automating Dependabot with GitHub Actions" e do `dependabot-auto-merge.yml` da frota.
2. Ao atualizar o arquivo (bump, starter, nova onda), não remover essas condições.
3. Canário: `@claude review` do operador numa PR do Dependabot gera job "skipped".

Relacionadas: [[feedback-claude-pr-review-always-inline-threads]], [[feedback-dependabot-fully-automatic-islands-native-only]].

questions.question: Pôr AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md nos arquivos *ignore só tem efeito se os dois arquivos também saírem do controle do Git em cada repositório (git rm --cached; a cópia local continua no disco, intacta). Hoje eles estão versionados em 21 repositórios. Ao removê-los, o remoto perde o conteúdo, inclusive as seções próprias (ex.: gates e release do cross-review). E o @claude que roda no GitHub Actions (claude.yml) deixa de achar o CLAUDE.md no checkout e perde a seção 'Running in GitHub Actions'. Exemplo: um '@claude' numa PR do cross-review amanhã rodaria sem instrução nenhuma do repositório. Como seguir?

options.label: Ignorar e tirar do Git (Recommended)
options.description: Uma PR por repositório: adiciona /AGENTS.md e /CLAUDE.md ao .gitignore e a todo *ignore já existente na raiz (.npmignore, .prettierignore etc.) e remove os dois do versionamento. É o mesmo modelo do .github-private. A cópia local fica intacta e deixa de aparecer como alterada. O remoto e o @claude da CI ficam sem esses arquivos.

options.label: Só adicionar aos *ignore
options.description: Adiciona as entradas aos *ignore sem tirar os arquivos do Git. Os arquivos continuam versionados com o conteúdo antigo no remoto e seguem aparecendo como alterados localmente: na prática, as entradas não têm efeito.

options.label: Ignorar, tirar do Git, mover seções
options.description: Igual à primeira opção, mas as seções próprias de cada repositório e a de GitHub Actions vão, sem alteração, para um arquivo versionado novo (ex.: docs/agent-repo-notes.md), e o claude.yml passa a apontar para ele. Preserva o conteúdo e a CI, mas mexe nos workflows.

input.description:
## Decisão do operador (05/11/2026)

Pedido feito junto com a auditoria LCV-557 + LCV-574, mas é uma frente independente: abrir um PR pronto (não rascunho) por repositório para publicar o `AGENTS.md` e o `CLAUDE.md`. Até 05/11/2026 a cópia local desses arquivos não estava sincronizada com o `main` remoto.

Decisões, na ordem em que foram tomadas:

1. **Conteúdo:** "Mestre + seções do repo". Cada arquivo recebe o texto-mestre do workspace inteiro e, ao final, as seções próprias daquele repositório, copiadas sem alteração. Dentro de cada repositório, `AGENTS.md` e `CLAUDE.md` ficam iguais.
2. **Repositórios públicos** (`.github` e `lcv-leo/lcv-leo`): "Publicar igual nos públicos".
3. "Publica tudo e sincroniza a main remota com o local com a decisão que tomei frente as opções que você me deu na primeira vez."
4. "E também remover os que estão na main remota": remover as entradas `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` dos arquivos `*ignore` do `main` remoto. """LCV-577: prepare one worktree per repository with the master text plus the
repository's own sections, and drop AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md entries from *ignore files."""
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

WS = Path(r"C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace")
WT_ROOT = WS / ".worktrees"
BRANCH = "claude/lcv-577-sync-agent-instructions"
BLOCK = "<!-- entire-agent:begin -->"
RUNNING = "## Running in GitHub Actions"
IGNORE_ENTRIES = frozenset({"AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md", "/AGENTS.md", "/CLAUDE.md"})
REPOS = (
    ".github-org", ".github-private", "admin-app", "astrologo-android", "astrologo-app",
    "astrologo-ios", "calculadora-android", "calculadora-app", "calculadora-ios",
    "cross-review", "github-operations", "lcv-leo", "maestro-android", "maestro-app",
    "maestro-ios", "mainsite-app", "mtasts-motor", "oraculo-financeiro",
    "programa-android", "programa-ios", "sponsor-motor", "ultrabrain-mcp",
)


def git(repo: Path, *args: str, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[bytes]:
    result = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), *args], capture_output=True)
    if check and result.returncode != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(f"git {' '.join(args)} in {repo}: {result.stderr.decode(errors='replace')}")
    return result


def remote_text(repo: Path, name: str) -> str | None:
    result = git(repo, "show", f"origin/main:{name}", check=False)
    return result.stdout.decode("utf-8") if result.returncode == 0 else None


def own_sections(repo: Path) -> str:
    """Repository-owned text: AGENTS.md before the managed block, plus the CLAUDE.md
    'Running in GitHub Actions' section. The generic Entire section and the old
    CLAUDE.md preamble are covered by the master text and are left out on purpose."""
    parts: list[str] = []
    agents = remote_text(repo, "AGENTS.md")
    if agents is not None and BLOCK in agents:
        head = agents.split(BLOCK, 1)[0].rstrip()
        if head:
            parts.append(head)
    claude = remote_text(repo, "CLAUDE.md")
    if claude is not None and RUNNING in claude:
        running = RUNNING + claude.split(RUNNING, 1)[1].split(BLOCK, 1)[0]
        parts.append(running.rstrip())
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def strip_ignore(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    raw = path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    newline = "\r\n" if "\r\n" in raw else "\n"
    lines = raw.split(newline)
    kept = [line for line in lines if line.strip() not in IGNORE_ENTRIES]
    removed = [line for line in lines if line.strip() in IGNORE_ENTRIES]
    if removed:
        path.write_bytes(newline.join(kept).encode("utf-8"))
    return removed


def prepare(name: str, master: str) -> dict[str, object]:
    repo = WS / name
    wt = WT_ROOT / f"{name.lstrip('.')}-lcv577"
    if wt.exists():
        raise RuntimeError(f"worktree already exists: {wt}")
    git(repo, "worktree", "add", "-b", BRANCH, str(wt), "origin/main")
    sections = own_sections(repo)
    content = master.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
    if sections:
        content += "\n---\n\n" + sections + "\n"
    for target in ("AGENTS.md", "CLAUDE.md"):
        (wt / target).write_bytes(content.encode("utf-8"))
    ignore_changes: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    tracked = git(wt, "ls-files").stdout.decode("utf-8").splitlines()
    for rel in tracked:
        if Path(rel).name.startswith(".") and Path(rel).name.endswith("ignore"):
            removed = strip_ignore(wt / rel)
            if removed:
                ignore_changes[rel] = removed
    return {
        "repo": name,
        "worktree": str(wt),
        "own_sections_lines": len(sections.splitlines()) if sections else 0,
        "ignore_changes": ignore_changes,
    }


def main() -> int:
    master = (WS / "CLAUDE.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
    if master != (WS / "AGENTS.md").read_bytes().decode("utf-8"):
        raise RuntimeError("workspace AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md differ; master text is ambiguous")
    report = [prepare(name, master) for name in REPOS]
    print(json.dumps(report, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

$branch = 'claude/lcv-577-sync-agent-instructions'
foreach ($wt in Get-ChildItem "$ws\.worktrees" -Directory -Filter '*-lcv577') {
    Push-Location $wt.FullName
    $slug = ((git remote get-url origin) -replace '^.*github\.com[:/]', '' -replace '\.git$', '')
    $checkpoint = (@(git log -1 --format='%(trailers:key=Entire-Checkpoint,valueonly)') | Where-Object { $_.Trim() } | Select-Object -First 1)
    $pr = gh pr list --repo $slug --head $branch --state all --json number,isDraft,autoMergeRequest,headRefOid,labels,state --jq '.[0] | "#\(.number) state=\(.state) draft=\(.isDraft) automerge=\(.autoMergeRequest != null) head=\(.headRefOid) labels=\([.labels[].name] | join(","))"'
    $remoteHead = (git ls-remote origin "refs/heads/$branch") -split "`t" | Select-Object -First 1
    $ref = if ($checkpoint) { [bool](git ls-remote origin 'refs/entire/checkpoints/*' | Select-String -SimpleMatch $checkpoint.Trim()) } else { $false }
    '{0,-40} local={1} remote={2} sig={3} cp={4} cpRefOrigin={5} PR: {6}' -f $slug, (git rev-parse --short=12 HEAD), ($remoteHead ? $remoteHead.Substring(0, 12) : 'NONE'), (git log -1 --format='%G?'), $checkpoint, $ref, $pr
    Pop-Location
}

Tarefa SOMENTE LEITURA (nenhum git commit/push, nenhum `entire trail finding resolve`, nenhum comentário em PR). Objetivo: inventário COMPLETO de todos os trails do Entire que tenham findings, em toda a frota LCV Ideas & Software.

Frota (22 repositórios, todos com branch main): LCV-Ideas-Software/{mainsite-app, astrologo-app, calculadora-app, oraculo-financeiro, admin-app, mtasts-motor, maestro-app, .github, cross-review, sponsor-motor, ultrabrain-mcp, .github-private, github-operations, programa-android, calculadora-android, maestro-android, astrologo-android, programa-ios, maestro-ios, calculadora-ios, astrologo-ios} e lcv-leo/lcv-leo. Clones locais em C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\<nome> (o repo .github está na pasta .github-org).

Como executar:
- Descubra a sintaxe exata com `entire agent-help trail`, `entire agent-help trail list`, `entire agent-help trail finding` e `entire agent-help trail finding list` (não adivinhe flags). Use --json e --no-pager quando existirem. Comandos `entire` que precisem de autenticação, e qualquer `gh`, devem rodar pelo terminal persistente: python C:/Users/lcvle/lcv-workspace/github-operations/tools/op-terminal/opx.py --terminal default --shell pwsh --timeout <=600 -f <script.ps1>. Escreva os scripts em C:/Users/lcvle/lcv-workspace/github-operations/temp/lcv-574/trails/. O terminal é uma fila serial compartilhada: agrupe tudo em poucos scripts grandes, sem laços de espera.
- Uma observação anterior indicou ~428 trails com status open no projeto gh/LCV-Ideas-Software e que a listagem pode vir marcada isPossiblyPartial=true: pagine até o fim (cursor/página) e, se a listagem for parcial, contorne consultando por repositório e por número de trail. Leia os findings de TODOS os trails (abertos e fechados), não só dos que têm change aberta. A célula de jurisdição pode importar (houve 'repo not in this region' na célula br; a us respondeu) — use --jurisdiction/-j quando a ajuda indicar.
- Para cada finding NÃO resolvido, retorne: repo, número do trail, título, branch/PR GitHub correspondente e seu estado atual (open/merged/closed, via gh), ID do finding, severidade, arquivo e linha, texto integral do finding, e se o problema ainda existe no main atual (abra o arquivo em origin/main pelo clone local após `git fetch` e confira; diga 'ainda se aplica', 'já corrigido no main (prova: linha/SHA)' ou 'código não existe mais').
- Também liste a contagem de findings já resolvidos por repo (só números).

Entregue no final um relatório em português do Brasil, organizado por repositório, com a tabela de findings não resolvidos e as provas. Ao terminar, apague a pasta C:/Users/lcvle/lcv-workspace/github-operations/temp/lcv-574/trails/ e confirme a ausência.

O que está quebrado é só o **caminho de publicação**. O deploy de 05/11 não conseguiu construir a imagem nova, porque a imagem-base `runtime-audit` fixada por digest foi apagada do Artifact Registry. Os três serviços seguem na revisão anterior, que funciona, mas a próxima versão do backend (com o `google-genai` 1.80.0 e qualquer correção futura) não sobe até a base ser reconstruída e repinada. Lembrando a regra do produto: o Oráculo não tem usuários, então isso não afeta ninguém hoje. É um bloqueio de entrega, não de operação.

O agente que investiga essa imagem vai devolver como ela é construída e o caminho nativo do próprio repositório para reconstruí-la. Com isso aplico a correção. A preparação das correções nos 22 repositórios segue rodando.

result.output:
# Cloud Run runtime provenance

The HTTP and job Dockerfiles consume this immutable, CMEK-protected Artifact
Registry runtime:

`us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/lcv-ideas-and-software/astrologo-paid-cmek/runtime-audit@sha256:9d0fc0a95628575f6ff4c5151c1b99aac61f93050a290faf9305387646078895`

Despite its historical package name, every digest in `runtime-audit` that a
Dockerfile references is a production dependency. **Do not delete it.** Before
removing any image from this registry, search the repository for its digest
(`grep -rn "<digest>" .`) and check Cloud Run services, jobs and revisions: on
29/10/2026 the previous runtime digest was deleted while closing a Security
Command Center finding after checking only Cloud Run, and the next deployment
failed at `FROM` with `manifest unknown` (LCV-464). No local `temp/` path is
needed to build the staged application containers.

## What the runtime is and why

The runtime is the official Docker Hub image
`eclipse-temurin:25.0.5_8-jre-alpine-3.24`, linux/amd64 manifest
`sha256:a5ae9049a626d248082d8b1f2c8dfa0b9c5f0b376243d5100ded5ba5fefea276`
(published 29/10/2026), with a single change made by this directory's
[Dockerfile](Dockerfile): `libexpat` goes from `2.9.0-r0` to Alpine 3.24's
`2.10.0-r0`, which fixes CVE-2026-115506 and CVE-2026-113351 (HIGH) and
CVE-2026-117610 and CVE-2026-118370 (MEDIUM). `libexpat` is in the image only
as a dependency of `fontconfig`. On 02/11/2026 Artifact Analysis started
reporting these CVEs in every image built on the unchanged official digest,
the deployment refuses any image with a known vulnerability, and no official
Temurin Alpine image carried the fix. The operator authorized this derived base
on 02/11/2026 as a case-by-case exception to the no-customization rule
(LCV-448). The image carries Alpine 3.24.3 with `brotli-libs-1.2.1-r0`,
`openssl-3.5.9-r0`, `musl-1.2.6-r3`, `zlib-1.3.2-r1` and `libexpat-2.10.0-r0`
(the adopted digest's Artifact Analysis package list), and the official
image's unchanged Temurin-25.0.5+8.

## Build and adoption

Native Cloud Build builds [Dockerfile](Dockerfile) with the same build account,
region and CMEK source and log bucket as the deployment's own image builds:

```text
gcloud builds submit backend/container --project lcv-ideas-and-software --region us-central1 --tag us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/lcv-ideas-and-software/astrologo-paid-cmek/runtime-audit:temurin-25.0.5-8-jre-alpine-3.24-libexpat-2.10.0-r0-20261102 --service-account projects/lcv-ideas-and-software/serviceAccounts/astrologo-paid-builder@lcv-ideas-and-software.iam.gserviceaccount.com --gcs-source-staging-dir gs://run-sources-lcv-ideas-and-software-us-central1/services/astrologo-paid/runtime-base/staging --gcs-log-dir gs://run-sources-lcv-ideas-and-software-us-central1/services/astrologo-paid/runtime-base/logs
```

The build of 02/11/2026 logged `(1/1) Upgrading libexpat (2.9.0-r0 ->
2.10.0-r0)` and pushed the digest above under that tag. The exact version pin
makes a rebuild fail if Alpine no longer serves that release. A digest is
adopted only after Artifact Analysis completes its automatic scan with no
vulnerability occurrences: this one finished (`FINISHED_SUCCESS`) at
2026-11-02T15:54:49Z with zero vulnerabilities and `libexpat 2.10.0-r0`.

## Returning to the official image

The exception ends when the official `eclipse-temurin` 25 JRE Alpine image
ships `libexpat` 2.10.0-r0 or later; the rebuild was requested in
[docker-library/official-images#22648](https://github.com/docker-library/official-images/issues/22648).
Then mirror that official digest unchanged, as from 29/10 to 02/11/2026, with
the single `gcrane copy` recipe kept in history
(`git show b9c182c:backend/container/cloudbuild.yaml`), its upstream digest
and dated tag updated. Scan the mirror, point both application Dockerfiles at
it and delete this directory's `Dockerfile`.

History of the base: until 29/10/2026, `18e25de9…`, built from the official
Temurin 25.0.4.1 image (`08919efb…`) with `brotli-libs` upgraded and the JRE
replaced by the official 25.0.5+8 archive (both digests deleted on
29/10/2026); from 29/10 to 02/11/2026, the official `a5ae9049…` mirrored
unchanged (tag `temurin-25.0.5-8-jre-alpine-3.24-20261029`); since 02/11/2026,
the derived base above.

Temurin/OpenJDK uses GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception and includes additional
supplier notices under `/opt/java/openjdk/legal/`; the complete archive retains
them. See [Adoptium licenses](https://adoptium.net/docs/licenses). Alpine
packages retain their published license metadata; Brotli and Expat use the MIT
license ([Brotli](https://github.com/google/brotli/blob/master/LICENSE),
[Expat](https://github.com/libexpat/libexpat/blob/master/expat/COPYING)).
The pinned upstream runtime and JRE archives remain available from their
supplier releases and the private CMEK registry. The HTTP launcher's separate
authorized dependency rebuild is documented in [framework/NOTICE.md](../framework/NOTICE.md).

## Registry cleanup: the serving and rollback tags

Since 02/11/2026 (operator decision) the repository `astrologo-paid-cmek` has
three native cleanup policies:

| Policy | Action | Condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `keep-runtime-base` | keep | package name prefix `runtime-audit` |
| `keep-serving-and-rollback` | keep | tag prefix `serving` or `rollback` |
| `delete-after-3-days` | delete | any version older than 3 days |

A version that matches a keep policy is kept
([cleanup policies](https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/repositories/cleanup-policy-overview)),
so every `astrologo-paid` and `astrologo-paid-runner` image that holds neither
tag is deleted three days after upload, including the run tags
(`r<run id>-<attempt>`) of earlier deployments. The last step of a successful

TaskStop (ou o fim da sessão) numa tarefa de segundo plano que roda `opx.py "python -I script.py"` encerra só o processo bash/opx que chamou o script. O `python.exe` executado dentro do terminal persistente `op run` continua rodando.

**Why:** em 25/10/2026, na LCV-448, eu disse ao operador e registrei na issue, às 16:47, que o vigia do backup do Firestore estava "desligado". Às 22:50 o `Win32_Process` mostrou o vigia (desde 14:36) e mais dois scripts ainda vivos. Não houve dano só porque o `policy_edit.py` que ele chamaria já tinha sido apagado. A afirmação, porém, era falsa e precisou de errata pública.

**How to apply:**
1. Depois de qualquer TaskStop em tarefa lançada pelo opx, rodar `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process -Filter "Name='python.exe'" | Where-Object { $_.CommandLine -match '<pasta ou script>' }` e encerrar o que sobrar com `Stop-Process -Id <pid> -Force`.
2. Só afirmar "desligado" depois de a releitura dar 0 processos.
3. Uma pasta `temp/` que recusa `rm -rf` com "Device or resource busy" é sinal de processo vivo usando o script.

Relacionadas: [[feedback_every_key_dependent_command_goes_through_the_opx_terminal]], [[feedback_work_temp_folder_inside_repo_delete_at_end]], [[feedback_pending_or_blocked_claims_require_irrefutable_proof_and_prior_research]].

Com uma exceção, que já está sendo corrigida: **sim**, todas as Actions de todos os repositórios estão na versão mais recente. A prova vem do `origin/main` lido agora há pouco, em 05/11/2026.

**Varredura ao vivo:**
- **657 usos** de Actions externas, nos **22 repositórios**, cobrindo **22 Actions** diferentes. Cada pin foi comparado com o SHA da release estável mais recente.
- Todos estão pinados por **SHA completo** e com comentário de versão. Não há nenhum pin por tag.
- Nenhuma Action ficou para trás. Os três casos que pareciam divergentes foram resolvidos:
  - **`github/codeql-action` v4.39.3** (`33d7b85d…`) é a versão mais nova da Action. Pelo `src/defaults.json` da própria versão pinada, ela já usa por padrão o motor **CodeQL 2.27.4** (`bundleVersion: codeql-bundle-v2.27.4`), o mesmo do changelog que você mandou (04/11/2026). Não há bump pendente para receber o 2.27.4.
  - **`anthropics/claude-code-action`** está em v1.0.268 (`c0949c50…`), a mais nova.
  - **`google-github-actions/auth`** está em v3.0.0 (`7c6bc770…`). É a última release com número de versão; a `v3` posterior é só a tag móvel que aponta para o mesmo commit.
- Não há nenhum PR do Dependabot de Actions aberto.

**A exceção:**
- O **template do Scorecard** no repositório `.github` (`workflow-templates/scorecard.yml:58`) ainda fixa o CodeQL v4.39.2. É o modelo usado para criar workflows em repositórios novos, não um workflow em execução. O Dependabot não cobre essa pasta. A correção para v4.39.3 já está na preparação do PR do `.github`.

**O que acompanha isso:**
- Em 15 repositórios, o inventário `THIRDPARTY.md` ainda cita o CodeQL v4.39.2, porque os merges automáticos do Dependabot não atualizam esse documento. Isso também entra nos PRs em preparação.
